description: A curated catalogue of 35 Ayurveda-inspired, practical daily activities for a prototype personalised Dincharya recommendation feature.

dosha_affinity_scale.note: These are heuristic product-design labels, not clinically validated dosha-effect scores or medical recommendations.

selection_notes: Use the user's stored Prakriti classification as an input to recommendation logic.
For mixed Prakriti profiles, combine or weight the relevant dosha affinity values; do not treat the heuristic scores as clinical evidence.
Time availability must be checked against duration_minutes before a task is selected.
Medical-condition and safety screening must be applied separately from Prakriti matching.
The catalogue contains traditional practices and modern adaptations; ayurvedic_principle describes the inspiration and does not claim proven clinical efficacy.
The catalogue does not diagnose, treat, or replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional.

tasks.title: Mindful Breathing
tasks.description: Pause work, sit comfortably, and breathe naturally with relaxed attention. Do not force or hold the breath.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by pranayama and cultivation of mental calm; this is gentle breath awareness, not a therapeutic breathing protocol.
safety_restrictions: Stop if dizzy, breathless, or uncomfortable.
Do not use forced breathing or breath retention.
source_references: Charaka Samhita Online - Dinacharya (traditional daily-regimen context)
NCCIH - Ayurvedic Medicine: In Depth (evidence and safety context)

tasks.title: Gentle Neck and Shoulder Stretches
tasks.description: Slowly roll the shoulders and gently move the neck through a comfortable range without pulling or forcing.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern adaptation of gentle movement and vyayama; not a classical named Dinacharya procedure.
safety_restrictions: Avoid circles or movements that cause neck pain.
Stop if pain, tingling, or dizziness occurs.

tasks.title: Comfortable Water Pause
tasks.description: Take a brief pause to drink water according to thirst and personal fluid needs. Warm or room-temperature water is optional.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by traditional attention to drinking habits and Ushapana; hydration needs vary and warm water is not universally required.
safety_restrictions: Do not force excess water.
Users with clinician-prescribed fluid restrictions should follow that advice.

tasks.title: Screen and Eye Rest
tasks.description: Look away from the screen at a distant object, blink naturally, and relax the face. Keep the eyes open or closed comfortably.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: A modern screen-break adaptation; it should not be presented as a treatment for eye disorders.
safety_restrictions: Do not press or rub the eyes.
Seek appropriate eye care for persistent pain or visual changes.

tasks.title: Short Mindful Walk
tasks.description: Walk at an easy, comfortable pace while paying attention to steps and surroundings.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by vihara and moderate vyayama; pace should be adapted to the individual.
safety_restrictions: Use a safe, accessible route.
Adapt or skip if walking is restricted or causes symptoms.

tasks.title: Seated Spinal Mobility
tasks.description: Sit upright and gently lengthen the spine; make small, comfortable torso movements without forcing a twist.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern gentle-movement adaptation inspired by vyayama and yoga.
safety_restrictions: Avoid twisting or bending that causes pain.
Skip if advised to restrict spinal movement.

tasks.title: Quiet Mindful Pause
tasks.description: Step away from active work, sit quietly, and notice sounds and bodily sensations without trying to change them.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by sattva-oriented mental discipline; a contemporary mindfulness adaptation.
safety_restrictions: If stillness increases distress, switch to a grounding activity such as looking around or walking.
source_references: Charaka Samhita Online - Dinacharya (general daily-regimen context)

tasks.title: Standing Stretch and Movement
tasks.description: Stand if comfortable, gently reach upward, move the ankles, and take a few relaxed steps.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern brief vyayama-inspired movement break.
safety_restrictions: Use support if balance is limited.
Skip movements that cause pain or dizziness.

tasks.title: Gentle Abhyanga Self-Massage
tasks.description: If suitable, gently massage a small area such as hands, feet, or limbs using a skin-compatible oil, then wash off as preferred.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Abhyanga is a traditional Ayurvedic oil-massage practice associated with Dinacharya.
safety_restrictions: Avoid with oil allergy, irritated or broken skin, or where a clinician has advised against massage.
Use a small patch test first.
Avoid slipping; clean oil from floors.

tasks.title: Pada Abhyanga-Inspired Foot Massage
tasks.description: Gently massage the feet with clean hands; optional use of a suitable, skin-compatible oil. Keep pressure light.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by Pada Abhyanga, the traditional practice of foot oil massage.
safety_restrictions: Avoid on wounds, infection, reduced foot sensation, or inflamed skin.
Avoid oil if it creates a slipping risk.

tasks.title: Relaxed Evening Walk
tasks.description: Take an easy walk in a safe place, at a pace that allows comfortable conversation.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by moderate vihara and vyayama; avoid overexertion.
safety_restrictions: Choose a safe route and suitable weather.
Adapt to mobility, cardiovascular, or other medical restrictions.

tasks.title: Dynamic Mobility Routine
tasks.description: Perform gentle, controlled movements such as shoulder rolls, ankle mobility, and comfortable arm and leg movements.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern adaptation of vyayama and yoga-based movement.
safety_restrictions: Keep movements pain-free.
Avoid vigorous exercise close to bedtime if it disrupts sleep.

tasks.title: Mindful Nature Walk
tasks.description: Walk in a safe outdoor or green space and gently notice the surroundings without rushing.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern vihara-inspired routine combining gentle movement and a calming environment.
safety_restrictions: Consider air quality, heat, allergies, daylight, and personal safety.
Use an indoor alternative when needed.

tasks.title: Gentle Yoga Practice
tasks.description: Choose a short sequence of comfortable, beginner-friendly yoga postures and move without strain.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Yoga is a traditional mind-body discipline used here as a gentle daily movement option.
safety_restrictions: Avoid advanced postures and painful ranges.
Adapt for pregnancy, injuries, balance issues, or clinician-directed restrictions.

tasks.title: Comfortable Bathing Ritual
tasks.description: Take a comfortable bath or shower as part of a regular personal-care routine; avoid extremes of water temperature.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Snana (bathing) is described within traditional daily-regimen practices; temperature preference should be individualised.
safety_restrictions: Avoid very hot water, especially with heat sensitivity or certain skin conditions.
Use non-slip surfaces.

tasks.title: Gentle Scalp Massage
tasks.description: Use fingertips to gently massage the scalp without scratching or applying strong pressure; oil is optional.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by traditional head-oil and self-care practices; this simple version does not claim therapeutic effects.
safety_restrictions: Avoid with scalp infection, irritation, open lesions, or sensitivity to oils.
Stop if discomfort occurs.

tasks.title: Relaxing Music Pause
tasks.description: Listen to calm or personally enjoyable music at a comfortable volume while resting.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: A contemporary sensory-rest practice inspired by the Ayurvedic emphasis on balanced sensory experience.
safety_restrictions: Keep volume comfortable.
Choose music that feels calming rather than overstimulating.
source_references: Charaka Samhita Online - Dinacharya (general lifestyle context)

tasks.title: Gentle Foot Massage
tasks.description: Gently massage the feet with clean hands; optional use of a small amount of suitable skin-compatible oil.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by Pada Abhyanga, a traditional foot-massage practice.
safety_restrictions: Avoid on wounds, infection, inflamed skin, or feet with reduced sensation.
Prevent slipping if oil is used.

tasks.title: Screen-Free Wind-Down
tasks.description: Put away phones and other screens for a short period before bed and choose a quiet offline activity.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern adaptation supporting a regular Ratricharya and sleep routine.
safety_restrictions: Adapt the routine where screens are required for accessibility or essential needs.

tasks.title: Gentle Bedtime Stretching
tasks.description: Try a few comfortable stretches for the back, shoulders, or legs, keeping the movements slow and easy.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Gentle yoga-inspired movement adapted for the nighttime routine.
safety_restrictions: Avoid strenuous or painful stretches.
Skip movements restricted by a clinician.

tasks.title: Gentle Alternate-Nostril Breathing
tasks.description: If already familiar and comfortable, practise slow, unforced alternate-nostril breathing without breath retention. Otherwise use natural breath awareness.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Nadi Shodhana is a traditional pranayama practice; this entry is a gentle, non-retentive adaptation.
safety_restrictions: Do not force airflow or hold the breath.
Skip if nasal blockage, respiratory discomfort, dizziness, or anxiety occurs.

tasks.title: Gratitude Reflection
tasks.description: Recall or write down one or two things you appreciated about the day, without pressuring yourself to feel positive.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern reflective practice inspired by mental steadiness and sattva-oriented conduct.
safety_restrictions: If reflection becomes distressing, stop and choose a neutral calming activity.

tasks.title: Quiet Meditation
tasks.description: Sit or lie comfortably and observe natural breathing or bodily sensations for a few minutes.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by dhyana and traditional mind-training practices.
safety_restrictions: If meditation increases distress, stop and use an eyes-open grounding activity.

tasks.title: Quiet Reading
tasks.description: Read a few pages of light, non-work-related material in comfortable lighting.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern wind-down habit compatible with a regular nighttime regimen.
safety_restrictions: Avoid material that is stimulating or stressful.
Use comfortable lighting.

tasks.title: Prepare Tomorrow's Essentials
tasks.description: Set out essential items for the next day and write down only the most important priorities.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern routine-building practice that supports regularity and reduces last-minute demands.
safety_restrictions: Keep planning brief; stop if it becomes a source of worry or work-related stimulation.

tasks.title: Consistent Bedtime Ritual
tasks.description: Follow the same simple sequence each night, such as washing up, dimming lights, and getting into bed at a consistent time.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by Ratricharya and regular daily rhythm; modern sleep guidance also supports consistent schedules.
safety_restrictions: Adapt timing to work, caregiving, and medical needs; do not sacrifice adequate sleep to follow a rigid schedule.

tasks.title: Morning Water Pause (Ushapana-Inspired)
tasks.description: After waking, drink a comfortable amount of water if thirsty and if it fits your individual fluid needs.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by Ushapana, a traditional morning water practice; specific health benefits are not assumed.
safety_restrictions: Do not force large volumes.
Follow clinician advice if fluid intake is restricted.

tasks.title: Tongue Cleaning (Jihwa Nirlekhana)
tasks.description: Gently clean the tongue using a clean tongue scraper or toothbrush, without scraping hard.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Jihwa Nirlekhana is a traditional oral-hygiene practice included in descriptions of Dinacharya.
safety_restrictions: Use gentle pressure and a clean tool.
Stop if soreness, bleeding, or irritation occurs.

tasks.title: Gentle Morning Stretching
tasks.description: Begin with easy shoulder, ankle, and full-body stretches within a comfortable range.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by gentle vyayama and yoga-based movement.
safety_restrictions: Avoid bouncing or forcing stretches.
Adapt for injuries or mobility restrictions.

tasks.title: Modified Surya Namaskar
tasks.description: Practise a few slow, modified rounds of Surya Namaskar only if familiar and physically comfortable; a gentle mobility sequence is an alternative.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Traditional yoga sequence commonly used as a morning movement practice; intensity must be individualised.
safety_restrictions: Not suitable for everyone; adapt or omit for injuries, pregnancy, balance issues, or medical restrictions.
Avoid pushing through pain, dizziness, or breathlessness.

tasks.title: Morning Meditation
tasks.description: Sit comfortably and spend a few minutes noticing natural breathing or setting a calm intention for the day.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by dhyana and sattva-oriented mental discipline.
safety_restrictions: If stillness is uncomfortable, try a short eyes-open grounding practice.

tasks.title: Gentle Pranayama or Breath Awareness
tasks.description: Practise calm, unforced breathing or simple breath awareness. Avoid rapid breathing and breath retention.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by pranayama; the catalogue uses a conservative beginner-friendly adaptation.
safety_restrictions: No forced breathing or breath retention.
Stop if dizzy, breathless, or uncomfortable.

tasks.title: Outdoor Daylight Pause
tasks.description: Spend a few minutes outdoors in ordinary daylight, without looking directly at the sun.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Modern circadian-routine adaptation; not a classical Ayurvedic treatment.
safety_restrictions: Never look directly at the sun.
Consider heat, UV exposure, air quality, and photosensitivity; use shade and sun protection as appropriate.

tasks.title: Morning Walk
tasks.description: Take a comfortable walk at a pace appropriate to your fitness and energy level.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Inspired by morning vihara and vyayama; duration and intensity should be individualised.
safety_restrictions: Choose a safe route and suitable weather.
Adapt to medical and mobility restrictions.

tasks.title: Morning Oral Hygiene and Gentle Rinsing
tasks.description: Brush teeth with fluoride toothpaste and rinse the mouth with clean water as part of morning hygiene.
tasks.ayurvedic_principle: Dantadhavana is a traditional daily oral-hygiene practice; this entry follows contemporary safe oral-care guidance.
safety_restrictions: Use a suitable toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste.
Do not use herbal powders or strong substances as substitutes for standard dental care.
